name: I Forgot to Remember to Forget

podcast.body: Reissued by RCA Records at the beginning of 1956 as his last Sun single, backed with "Mystery Train." With RCA's backing, the single performed significantly better than its original Sun release, hitting number one on the country charts. "With RCA's backing, the single did far better than it had on Sun, hitting number one on the country charts at the beginning of 1956."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: This song was the A-side of Elvis's fifth single for Sun Records. It was a country song "especially written for Elvis" and described as a "perfectly adequate country pop song." "The A-side of Elvis' fifth single for Sun Records was one of those country songs that had been written especially for Elvis."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
